description.narrative: There are enormous areas in Vietnam where agriculture is not in line with the prevailing water conditions or is adversely affecting the water conditions of other water users. Climate change and land subsidence due to groundwater extraction exacerbate this situation.Solutions from the following five categories are crucial:• reduction of groundwater extraction;• embracing salinity;• embracing controlled flooding and water retention;• improving water use efficiency and the value of water; and• improving the water cycle and clean process water.There are inspiring cases of how Dutch expertise in water management and agriculture has been applied in the agricultural sector worldwide to help promote sustainability. Examples range from techniques to improve freshwater storage, using satellite imaging and real-time information to stimulate efficient irrigation and crop management, developing water stress tolerant varieties, to approaches at a broader scale such as land use planning and management. This expertise is mobilized to address the challenges in water management and agricultural restructuring faced by Vietnam. The study aims to understand what business opportunities exist and identify leads to provide services and knowledge, export technology and materials and invest in the Vietnamese agriculture and water sector, as well as to examine the interest of the Dutch agricultural and water sector and to develop a sustainable agricultural sector in the Mekong Delta of Vietnam. Insight into developments, business leads and funding opportunities facilitate increased business activities between Dutch and Vietnamese companies) that emerge out of water interventions as outlined in the Mekong Delta Plan and Resolution 120.The study should result in specific business opportunities that result from the recent developments and transformations in Vietnam.
